title: [finding] The other four "v3.0.0 Deep Integration modules" in data-objectstack have no consumer outside their own tests either
body:
Found while executing the #4152 ruling (PR #4239). Filed unassigned, recording only — PD #10.

## Fact

`CloudOperations` was one of five things added to `@object-ui/data-objectstack` under the `// v3.0.0 Deep Integration modules` banner in `src/index.ts`. #4152 measured that one and retired it. While measuring its consumers I swept the siblings on the same criterion, and they land in the same place:

| exported symbol | module | references outside `packages/data-objectstack` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `IntegrationManager` | `src/integration.ts` | 0 |
| `SecurityManager` | `src/security.ts` | 0 |
| `createDefaultCanvasConfig` / `snapToGrid` / `calculateAutoLayout` | `src/studio.ts` | 0 |
| `validatePluginContract` / `generateContractManifest` | `src/contracts.ts` | 0 |

Measured over `packages/`, `apps/` and `examples/` (`.ts` / `.tsx`, excluding `node_modules`). Every reference to each of these names lives inside `data-objectstack` itself — the `index.ts` re-export and `src/v3-compat.test.ts`. No app, no other package, no example wires any of them.

## Why this is graded observation-class, and why it is NOT a repeat of #4152

The important difference, and the reason I am not proposing it follow #4152 out the door: **these are not phantom**. Each one does what it says locally, with no absent backend behind it — `SecurityManager.generateCSPHeader()` really composes a CSP header, `snapToGrid` really snaps, `validatePluginContract` really validates. There is no `client.something?.` optional chain into a namespace that does not exist, and nothing fabricates a success. #4152's sharp edge — a well-formed `deploymentId` handed back for work that never happened — has no analogue here.

So what is left is only the startup-focus question, which is a triage call and not a defect report: published surface of a released package, carrying no measured business pull. Nobody is bitten today, and no user-visible behaviour is wrong.

## Adjacent, same theme

`src/v3-compat.test.ts` is titled `v3.0.0 compatibility tests for @objectstack dependencies` and its top-level `describe` is `v3.0.0 Compatibility`, against a resolved `@objectstack` family of `17.0.0-rc.6`. This is the same stale-version-claim smell #4152 recorded for `cloud.ts`'s module header, minus the false capability claim — the tests do exercise real local code, they are just not testing compatibility with a v3 of anything. PR #4239 removed that file's cloud block but deliberately left the header alone as out of scope.

## Possible directions (left for triage)

- Leave as-is. Nothing is wrong, and a self-contained helper costs little to keep.
- Retire whichever of the four have no roadmap pull, on the same startup-focus reasoning as #4152 — but on the "no consumer" limb only, without the "fabricates success" limb that made #4152 urgent.
- Keep them and re-title the module banner and `v3-compat.test.ts` so neither claims a v3 that the family left long ago.

Refs #4152, PR #4239.
